info.title: Rdio Scanner API
info.description: The complete entry-point surface of the Rdio Scanner server: the administrator REST surface (authentication, whole-config access, per-section config endpoints, alerts, logs, password change, access user management), the two call ingestion endpoints, the call history endpoints (search, one call, one recording), the two static applications, and the two WebSocket surfaces. Admin REST auth: raw JWT in the Authorization header, no Bearer prefix; HTTP 401 on invalid/expired token. The ingestion endpoints authenticate with the key form field. The WebSocket surfaces are documented as components.x-websockets (OpenAPI 3.1 has no native WebSocket construct): the listener protocol on any path, chosen by the Upgrade header, and the administrator configuration socket on /api/admin/config. The listener protocol is reserved for Saubeo Solutions native applications per API_ACCESS_POLICY.md.

One page of the call history, filtered by system, talkgroup, talkgroup group, talkgroup tag, and day. The paging bounds and the day window are the listener history search’s own: a limit above the ceiling is answered as the ceiling, and a negative offset is answered as the start of the table. The criteria come back as they were asked for, not as this server used them, so a caller can tell which of its filters this server read.

200.description: One page of call history and the total the filters matched.

401.description: A restricted server: no access code, an access code it does not carry, an expired access, or an address that spent its access-code attempts.

405.description: Method not answered by this endpoint.

get.description: One recorded call in full: system, talkgroup, site, instant, the frequencies it was heard on, the units that spoke, the talkgroups it was patched to, and the name, type, and length of its recording. The recording’s bytes are not here: a metadata question is asked far more often than a recording is listened to, and a metadata answer carrying the recording makes every metadata answer a download. The recording is fetched at the audioUrl this answer names.

parameters.name: callId
parameters.description: The identifier the history row carries.

200.description: One recorded call, without its recording.

401.description: A restricted server: the caller proved nothing, and is not told what it is missing.

405.description: Method not answered by this endpoint.

get.description: The recording of one call, as the server stored it: the stored bytes, the stored type, and the name the recording was stored under. The recording lives in the database beside its call, so nothing is converted and no path is traversed. A range request is answered as the server answers a range for any other content. The caller’s access is checked before a single byte is read.

get.summary: Scanner webapp: the single-page application bundle
get.description: Every path that is not an /api path and not under /admin/ is answered by the scanner application: a request naming a bundle file gets the file, and every other request gets the application shell. A request carrying the Upgrade: websocket header is not the application at all: it is taken over as a listener connection (components.x-websockets.listener).

200.description: A bundle file, or the application shell for every route that is not a file.

get.summary: Administration subtree root: redirected to the trailing slash
get.description: The administration application is served from /admin/ and /admin itself is deliberately not registered: the mux redirects the subtree root by adding the trailing slash, which is what makes every relative URL in the admin shell resolve inside the admin bundle.

get.summary: Admin shell: the administration single-page application bundle
get.description: Every path under /admin/ that is not an API path is answered by the admin application: a request naming a bundle file gets the file, and every other request gets the application shell. A request carrying the Upgrade: websocket header is taken over as a listener connection (components.x-websockets.listener).

200.description: A bundle file, or the application shell for every route that is not a file.

adminJwt.name: Authorization
adminJwt.description: Raw JWT from POST /api/admin/login, no Bearer prefix. HS256, no expiry; the server keeps the last 5 issued tokens.

accessCode.name: X-Access-Code
accessCode.description: A listener access code, the same credential the listener socket asks a restricted server for. Accepted by the call history endpoints only, beside the administrator session. A server with no access list answers these endpoints to an anonymous caller. A code is a credential: the server never files one in its log, and refuses a guessing address once the address spent its attempts.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid, or expired token — the client must clear its session

SystemsScope.description: '*' means everything; otherwise a list of system ids or {id, talkgroups} objects

SystemRow.description: One system as the systems section saves it: the system row's own fields, its blacklist included. The sites, talkgroups, and units under a system belong to their own per-level endpoints; an entry that names them is read and ignored.

blacklists.description: The talkgroup references this system refuses: decimal references separated by commas, no spaces, empty for none. Saving the talkgroups level of this system stores the same field with the talkgroups.

TalkgroupsSave.description: The talkgroups of one system saved beside that system's blacklist: the rows, and the whole list as the section shows it. The rows and the list are stored in one save.

blacklists.description: The whole list, not a delta: decimal references separated by commas, no spaces, empty for none. A body that names it writes it; a body that does not, leaves the stored list alone.

AdminStatus.description: What this server is, what it is running right now, what it recorded over the last 24 hours, and what it lately complained about. Every list is answered as a list even when nothing was recorded.

server.description: The deployment and what this server can measure about itself.

docker.description: Whether the server thinks it is running in a container. The same answer the configuration read gives.

startedAt.description: The instant this server's start sequence ran, or the Unix epoch when it has not recorded one.

now.description: The instant the read ran, so that a page can tell how fresh the snapshot is.

uptimeSeconds.description: Whole seconds since startedAt, never negative, and 0 when no start was recorded.

baseDir.description: The folder the server was told to serve, or an empty string when the operator named none.

databaseBytes.description: The size of the file this server writes its database into. 0 when this deployment cannot state it.

databaseKnown.description: Whether this deployment can state the size at all. False on a backend whose data lives in a database server this one does not own.

live.description: What exists at the instant the read ran, and not what the configuration says should exist.

administratorSessions.description: The open administrator connections, the page reading this count among them.

dirwatchersRunning.description: The directory watchers actually watching right now: not the number configured, and not the number enabled.

heldCalls.description: The calls waiting out a hold right now.

audioConversion.description: Whether this deployment converts audio at all.

audioProbe.description: Whether this deployment measures the length of a recording at all.

activity.description: What this server recorded over the 24-hour window.

windowEnd.description: The end of the whole hour the read ran in, and not the instant it ran: two dashboards opened a second apart see the same buckets.

callsToday.description: Calls recorded since this server's own local midnight.

callsLastHour.description: Calls recorded in the rolling hour before the read ran. It can start mid-hour, and is not the current bucket.

lastCallAt.description: The instant of the most recent recorded call. Absent when the history is empty.

hours.description: The whole window, cut into 24 whole hours, oldest first. An hour with nothing in it is a zero and not a gap.

busiest.description: The five talkgroups with the most calls in the window, most first.

recent.description: The five most recent recorded calls, newest first, as summaries: never with the audio.

logs.description: What this server complained about over the last 24 hours.

windowStart.description: The instant 24 hours before the read ran.

sources.description: The subsystems that wrote an error or a warning, most trouble first. A subsystem that wrote neither is not named.

start.description: The instant the whole hour begins.

AdminStatusTalkgroup.description: One talkgroup's share of the window, named the way the configuration names it: the operator reads a talkgroup, and not a pair of references.

audioLengthSeconds.description: How long the recording lasts. The recording itself is not here: this read is asked every few seconds, and audio is the heaviest thing this server keeps.

CallsSearchRequest.description: The filters a call history search is asked with. Every field is optional; a field this server cannot read is left out of the echo it answers with.

system.description: Narrow the search to one system, named by the reference clients use.

talkgroup.description: With a system, narrow the search to one talkgroup on it.

group.description: A talkgroup group label: the search keeps the talkgroups it stands for.

tag.description: A talkgroup tag label: the search keeps the talkgroups it stands for.

date.description: The day the search is bounded to.

limit.description: Page size. Default 200, ceiling 500; a value outside them is clamped.

offset.description: Where to resume. A negative value is the start of the table.

CallsSearchResponse.description: One page of call history, the bounds the page spans, and the criteria as the caller asked for them.

count.description: How many calls the filters matched, not how many rows this page carries.

dateStart.description: The instant of the oldest call the page spans.

dateStop.description: The instant of the newest call the page spans.

CallSummary.description: One row of the call history: enough to name a call and ask for it. The recording is not here, and neither are the frequencies, units, and patches a full call carries.

system.description: The system reference the call was recorded on.

talkgroup.description: The talkgroup reference the call was recorded on.

audioLength.description: Length of the recording in seconds to the millisecond, when some source named it.

CallResponse.description: One recorded call. The recording’s bytes are deliberately absent: the name, the type, and the length of the recording are metadata and stay, and the bytes are fetched at audioUrl.

system.description: The system reference the call was recorded on.

talkgroup.description: The talkgroup reference the call was recorded on.

site.description: The site reference the call was recorded on, when the call names one.

delayed.description: The call is being held back by its talkgroup or system delay.

patches.description: The talkgroup references the call was patched to. A call read out of the history carries null.

audioName.description: The name the recording was stored under.

audioType.description: The MIME type the recording was stored with.

audioLength.description: Length of the recording in seconds to the millisecond, when some source named it.

audioUrl.description: Where to fetch the recording: GET /api/calls/{callId}/audio.

CallFrequency.description: One frequency the call was heard on, with what the receiver counted on it.

pos.description: The position of this frequency in the call, counting from zero.

errorCount.description: How many receiver errors were counted on this frequency.

spikeCount.description: How many spikes were counted on this frequency.

dbm.description: Signal level in dBm. A level of zero is not carried, and a negative one is not stored.

CallUnit.description: One unit that spoke in the call, named by the reference clients use.

pos.description: The position of this unit in the call, counting from zero.

listener.summary: Listener protocol: the connection the scanner webapp and the native applications hold
listener.description: Any path under / and /admin/ carrying the Upgrade: websocket header is taken over as a listener connection before anything is looked up. Frames are JSON arrays: [command, ...args]. A server with access codes asks for one (PIN) before answering anything else; a server with no access codes is open. Reserved for Saubeo Solutions and its native applications per API_ACCESS_POLICY.md.
listener.auth: The PIN command carries the access code when the server is restricted; no credential before it.

PIN.summary: Ask for an access code: refused, unlocked, and the configuration it unlocks.

CAL.summary: Fetch one recorded call in full, audio included, and push one that has just been recorded.

LCL.summary: Search one page of the recorded calls.

CFG.summary: Read the configuration this listener is allowed to see.

LFM.summary: Say which systems and talkgroups this listener wants live, and ack it.

LSC.summary: Report how many listeners are watching.

XPR.summary: The access code this listener unlocked has run out.

MAX.summary: This access code already has as many connections as it is allowed.

IOS.summary: For the iOS applications; never sent to a web client.

PID.summary: Push id, for the mobile applications; never sent to a web client.

adminConfig.summary: Administrator configuration socket: live configuration change announcements
adminConfig.description: The administration interface holds this connection open on the whole-configuration path to learn about configuration changes as they happen. The upgrade is refused on the per-section and per-level paths. The connection sends its raw JWT as the first frame and only ever reads afterwards; the server pushes the configuration after each change. The upgrader insists the connection comes from the same origin the page was served from.
adminConfig.auth: Raw JWT as the first frame; the connection is closed when the token is refused.
